title: Senior's toolkit: the right collection for the job
summary: Counter, defaultdict, deque, sorted with keys, heapq and bisect: the standard library pieces that replace hand-written loops.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the right collection for the job
steps.body: Most collection code at work is counting, grouping, top-N, sorting by a field or keeping the last few items. The standard library already does each of these, faster and with fewer bugs than a hand-written loop.

toolkit.what: Count things in one line, then ask for the most common.
flags: the 3 highest counts, as (item, count) pairs

toolkit.what: A dict that creates a missing value for you, so grouping needs no `if key not in d` check.
flags: turn it back into a plain dict before returning it

toolkit.what: A double-ended queue: adding or removing at either end is O(1). `list.pop(0)` is O(n).
Sort by any field. Python's sort is stable, so you can sort by several keys with a tuple.
flags: by dept, then highest salary first
by a dict key (`from operator import itemgetter`)

toolkit.what: The top N without sorting everything. `heappush` and `heappop` give you a priority queue.
Binary search in a sorted list: find the position for a value in O(log n), or insert keeping it sorted.
flags: insert and keep the list sorted

toolkit.what: Print nested dicts and lists readably, one item per line when it does not fit.
flags: sort keys (the default for `pp` is False)
toolkit.example:
from pprint import pp
pp(config, depth=2)

steps.explain: Ties in `most_common` keep first-seen order. `defaultdict(list)` creates an empty list the first time a length appears, and dicts keep insertion order.

steps.prompt: A log tailer keeps the last 1,000 lines in a list: `lines.append(l)` then `lines.pop(0)` when it is too long. The profiler says 90% of the time is in `pop`. What is the fix?
options: `recent = deque(maxlen=1000)` and just `recent.append(l)`: old lines fall off the left in O(1)
Switch to a `set`, which is faster
steps.explain: `list.pop(0)` shifts every remaining element, so it is O(n). A `deque` with `maxlen` drops the oldest item in constant time. `pop()` removes the newest line, which is the wrong one.

steps.prompt: `people` is a list of dicts. Sort it oldest first by the `"age"` key.
steps.explain: `itemgetter("age")` reads `p["age"]`; `attrgetter` reads an attribute, which dicts do not have. `reverse=True` puts the largest first.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before you write a loop that counts, groups or keeps a top N, ask which of `Counter`, `defaultdict`, `heapq` or `deque` already does it. In code review, `list.pop(0)` in a loop and a full sort just to take the first 10 are the two patterns to flag.
